name: Minimally invasive posterior approach to the calcaneus
corridor: Posterolateral para-Achilles interval through pre-Achilles fat to the superior calcaneus and posterior ankle/subtalar capsules

positioning.text: Position prone or lateral with the heel free, the Achilles relaxed when needed, and unobstructed access for posterior reduction and fluoroscopy.

setup.text: Assess posterior skin urgently because a displaced tuberosity fragment can threaten it; prepare percutaneous reduction tools, distractor options, and lateral and axial imaging.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the lateral Achilles border, calcaneal tuberosity, sural-nerve course, posterior ankle joint, and subtalar joint.

incision.text: Place a posterior incision adjacent to, but not directly over, the lateral border of the Achilles tendon; keep its superior extent posterior to the sural nerve.

superficial_interval.text: Deepen lateral to the Achilles paratenon through the pre-Achilles fat while preserving the tendon, paratenon, sural nerve, and lateral calcaneal vascular supply.

deep_interval.text: Continue to the superior calcaneus; vertical capsulotomies of the posterior ankle and subtalar joints can expose distal tibia, talus, and calcaneus, with distraction added when required.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with sural-nerve protection, lateral Achilles paratenon boundary, pre-Achilles fat, posterior joint capsules, and superior calcaneus.

structures_encountered.text: Achilles tendon and paratenon, sural nerve, lateral calcaneal artery territory, pre-Achilles fat, FHL medially, posterior ankle capsule, subtalar capsule, and tuberosity are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: The sural nerve, Achilles tendon and paratenon, lateral calcaneal artery, posterior skin, FHL, and posterior tibial neurovascular bundle are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Do not cross medially beyond the protective FHL plane toward the posterior tibial bundle, and do not place the incision directly over or violate the Achilles tendon.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid fixed pressure on the Achilles paratenon, posterior skin, and sural nerve; place any distractor under direct control to avoid talar or joint injury.

exposure.text: Exposes the superior and posterior calcaneus and, after capsulotomy, the posterior ankle and subtalar intervals for reduction and fixation.

limitations.text: Provides limited direct visualization of the lateral wall and anterior posterior facet; complex articular reconstruction may require another exposure.

extensions.text: A medial para-Achilles variant is possible but brings the posterior tibial neurovascular bundle closer and requires deliberate protection; add a lateral articular approach when needed.

indications.text: Use for selected simpler displaced intra- or extra-articular calcaneal patterns, particularly posterior tuberosity or tongue-type displacement amenable to posterior reduction and percutaneous fixation.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid as the sole exposure when complex posterior-facet or lateral-wall reconstruction requires direct visualization, or when the posterior wound corridor is compromised.

implant_implications.text: Plan posterior-to-anterior screws or other percutaneous constructs around the Achilles and joints, confirming adequate tuberosity purchase and avoiding plantar or articular penetration.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use lateral and axial heel views, supplemented by articular views, to verify tuberosity height, varus-valgus alignment, posterior-facet congruity, and screw containment.

closure.text: Close posterior capsules and deep tissue with absorbable suture as appropriate, preserve the paratenon, and perform tension-free skin closure.

complications.text: Complications include posterior skin necrosis, sural neuropathy, Achilles or paratenon injury, neurovascular injury, malreduction, joint penetration, nonunion, and subtalar arthritis.

bailouts.text: Urgently reduce a skin-threatening tuberosity even if definitive fixation must be staged; convert or add an articular exposure if reduction cannot be demonstrated safely.

procedure_applications.condition: A tuberosity, tongue-type, or selected simpler intra- or extra-articular pattern requires posterior reduction and percutaneous fixation

questions.question: Where should the posterior incision lie relative to the Achilles tendon?
questions.answer: Adjacent to its lateral border, not directly over the tendon.

questions.question: Which structure protects the posterior tibial neurovascular bundle medially?
questions.answer: The flexor hallucis longus muscle belly.

questions.question: What changes the timing priority for a calcaneal tuberosity fracture?
questions.answer: Posterior skin threat from the displaced fragment requires urgent reduction.
